b: He will take up the role in Jan 2027, with forestry competitiveness and the sector’s contribution to Finland’s economy among his priorities.
Jussi Vanhanen, president and CEO of Metsä Group (Image: Metsä Group)
Jussi Vanhanen, president and CEO of Metsä Group, has been elected chair of the Finnish Forest Industries Federation for 2027 at the organisation’s annual autumn meeting.
Vanhanen said the competitiveness of forestry and the forest industry, alongside the sector’s contribution to the Finnish economy, would be key priorities during his term.

“Finnish forestry competes first and foremost with fossil-based products. At the same time, the forest industry and forestry create significant value for Finnish society through jobs, tax revenue and indirect economic impacts. Their €17.4bn contribution to GDP and annual tax impact of €4bn support Finland’s prosperity,” he said.

He highlighted the high added value generated by the sector through the use of domestic raw materials, noting that its economic benefits extend to private forest owners and businesses operating within and around the forest industry.
“Ensuring the competitiveness of forestry is very much about ensuring Finland’s competitiveness,” Vanhanen said.
His term as chair will begin in Jan 2027.
